minimal_witness.preconditions: Frozen fanout with ordered child row IDs a<b; a completed, b running and provably stale under inclusive age; pageLimit=1,maxDrives=1; correct sorted bounded store query; no external releases/deletions. Child IDs here mean row ordering, not arbitrary domain record labels.
interleaving: Every runSchedulerTurn calls release with cursor:null; release page is only a, skips completed, returns done:false,cursor:a; turn discards those continuation fields.
Drive sweep obeys returned cursor: a replays; next page b is held because state running (staleness is not checked in driveChild); next empty page gives done:true but progress incomplete.
Caller resweeps from null while work remains: release again sees only a. b remains stale-running indefinitely absent another recovery actor.
minimal_witness.exact_observation: released=[] on every turn; b driven status held/detail running-held; full-cohort progress remains incomplete, not falsely completed.

counterevidence: releaseStaleFanoutClaims itself accepts cursor and returns honest cursor/done; a caller that separately advances that API across all pages can release b. It is not a helper bug.
Turn drive cursor accurately resumes processed rows; fresh running claims intentionally held. Do not blame drive-page honesty or require live claims to be cancelled.

External owner can perform full release sweeps, increase pageLimit beyond prefix, or remove terminal prefix. Those can remedy witness, but turn API neither exposes release continuation nor demonstrates such worker ownership.
Current test sweepToTerminal resets driving cursor only after done and checks progress; bounded finite loop is existing test source, not fresh witness execution.
reviews.permitted_ownership: Independent fair release driver is permitted, provided actual owner retains/advances its cursor and has eventual full frozen-row coverage. No choice of cursor persistence store, filtering schema or sweep schedule made.
reviews.required_fix_or_gate: Integrated scheduler must maintain full stale-claim coverage independent of terminal prefix (retain release continuation or equivalent proven driver). Preserve honest progress, bounded turn/page work and fresh-claim holding.
reviews.scope: Current TS exported scheduler + injected F7 serving surface; composition proves callability, not mounted deployment or incident. Memory and durable ordered-query stores both can exhibit stable-prefix starvation.

Synchronous append helper has no internal await; two calls in one JS isolate do not interleave its statements ordinarily. Witness is failure/restart or independent shared-port context, not imaginary scheduler preemption.

finalizeProviderOutput585-588 checks staged.length===received and exact original-byte prefix before append: the same crash drift refuses conflict there. Therefore LF02 is not a universal provider-output finalization vulnerability.
Missing counted staging, normal overdeclared append and actual policy cap failures already refuse. Native/plain-byte MIME validation and finalized digest recheck remain controls.
reviews.permitted_ownership: Atomic count+blob owner binding, idempotent offset/journal append or consistent guarded recovery can prevent drift. Mechanism choice not made; copy-returning persistent metadata is a scenario prerequisite, not a new port API requirement.
reviews.required_fix_or_gate: At direct completion/finalization, actual stored length must agree with received and declared length before usable immutable file. Crash after blob append/before metadata persistence cannot produce size/digest/content disagreement. Prove on actual independent persistent ports, not aliases.
reviews.separate_put_retry_limit: HTTP content route appends body then completes after every append; no offset/chunk identity exposed. Lost partial PUT then blind repeat can append again even without crash, but caller retry semantics/whole-file replacement/resume contract requires explicit decision. Do not collapse that question into the required length-agreement fix or assert all retries are promised idempotent.
reviews.scope: Supported TS append/complete APIs and authenticated HTTP adapter if injected matching kernel; production atomic/R2 join unresolved. ProviderOutput resume guard excludes its open-transfer path from basic retry witness.
